label: Makhan
note: Churned from dahi (set whole milk or malai), not from separated cream

about.text: The butter of the Indian subcontinent churned from dahi, set yoghurt made from whole milk or malai, rather than from fresh cream, traditionally by hand in an earthen pot. Eaten fresh, or heated slowly into desi ghee.

links.name: Journal of Food Science and Technology (2020)

sources.text: The photograph, its author and its licence, from its page.

how.label: set dahi, churn
how.text: Whole milk is soured into dahi with a spoonful of yesterday's dahi or chhach, and the lactic bacteria supply the diacetyl that gives makkhan its aroma. The whole curd, not separated cream, is churned, so makkhan keeps more moisture, curd and lactic acid than butter.

microbes.name: Lactococcus lactis subsp. lactis biovar diacetylactis

steps.note: Set at room temperature overnight with a spoonful of the previous day's dahi or chhach, best for churning at 0.9–1.1 % acidity and up to 2 % when uncontrolled.

steps.name: dilute
steps.note: The dahi is diluted with water.
Churned with a wooden beater in the morning.
